title: Machine learning derives a gene-mutation classifier predicting immunotherapy outcomes
summary: Multiple machine-learning approaches on nonsynonymous mutations identified key mutations tied to immune checkpoint blockade response and gave the Gene mutation-based Predictive Signature (GPS). GPS outperformed conventional predictors in independent cohorts, multiplex immunohistochemistry and multi-omics linked GPS groups to the lung adenocarcinoma tumor microenvironment, and groups responded differently in an ex vivo organoid-PBMC co-culture model.
ai_technology: Multiple machine-learning approaches for selecting a gene-mutation predictive signature (GPS)

evidence.tested: Independent clinical cohorts, multiplex immunohistochemistry and an ex vivo tumor organoid-PBMC co-culture.
evidence.unknown: Cohort sizes and effect sizes not read; the ex vivo model is small and the signature has not been tested in a trial; abstract only; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning selected the mutations that form the GPS classifier.
